comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C13, C22-C25. Both evaluations find PNab to be a well-validated pan-neuronal marker. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from multiple transgenic lines and counting methods, while peer reviewers highlight it as a novel and useful tool with 'outstanding imaging data' and 'convincing evidence.'

Perfect agreement on claims C14, C16, C28. Both evaluations support the finding that ectodermal and endodermal nerve nets are separate without connections. OpenEval notes the quantitative confocal data while acknowledging limited tissue sampling; peer reviewers identify this as a major finding with no concerns raised about the conclusion.

Perfect agreement on claims C15, C34-C38. Both evaluations support the finding that nerve nets consist of discrete bundles. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from confocal, TEM, and block face SEM; peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as a major finding with all three reviewers noting the bundle organization.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C40. Both evaluations support the differential association of nerve cells with muscle processes between ectoderm and endoderm. OpenEval cites convergent anatomical and quantitative evidence; peer reviewers explicitly note the close contacts in ectoderm versus endoderm without questioning the data.

Perfect agreement on claims C20-C21, C50-C52. Both evaluations support the lateral addition model for nerve net growth. OpenEval emphasizes grafting experiments with quantitative tracking; peer reviewers recognize the mechanism and its implications for neural communication without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C26-C27, C41. Both evaluations support the morphometric measurements. OpenEval notes consistency across imaging modalities; peer reviewers accept these measurements as part of the comprehensive anatomical characterization with 'outstanding imaging data.'

Disagreement on claims C86-C91 regarding PNab antigen identity. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing that cross-species validation logic is sound and PNab specificity is well-established even without knowing the antigen. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'the specificity of the antibody was not investigated' as an acknowledged limitation, though they accept the antibody's utility.

Agreement on claims C19, C46-C48, C94 regarding gap junctions and innexin expression. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes the inference about circuit-specific gap junctions lacks direct functional validation; peer reviewers accept the data as part of comprehensive characterization addressing cell communication without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C17, C29 regarding absence of endodermal nerve cells in tentacles. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval (R3) addresses broader distribution claims C17, C29-C33; peer reviewers (R4) focus specifically on C17, C29 as an 'unexpected' but well-supported major observation.

Partial overlap on claims C30-C33 regarding nerve cell distribution. Both evaluations support the quantitative characterization. OpenEval (R3) includes these with C17, C29 as semi-quantitative data; peer reviewers (R7) accept these as part of the comprehensive anatomical description without explicit concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C70-C71 regarding endodermal nerve net characteristics. Both evaluations support the observations. OpenEval (R10) addresses broader functional claims C69-C74, C76-C77 and notes speculation about osmotic sensing; peer reviewers (R11) focus on C70-C71 and accept the cautious functional speculation without questioning the characterization.
